title.narrative: Inclusive gender sensitive lifesaving multi-sectoral nutrition emergency response in affected communities of Michika, and Jere LGAs of Adamawa, and Borno state.

description.narrative: ltpgtThe lean season in Northeast Nigeria is driving sharp spikes in child malnutrition, while a global funding shortfall threatens the transition of existing facilities to under-resourced government systems. This heightens the risk of preventable child deaths, especially among with children 6-23m with severe and moderate acute malnutrition (SAM), who are at increased risk of death.ltbrgtTo address these challenges, CDHI proposes a six-month, inclusive gender-sensitive multi-sectoral nutrition and health response in Michika (Adamawa), and Jere (Borno). Leveraging CDHI’s experience and operational presence in the selected LGAs, the project will strengthen PHC’s nutrition and health service delivery to sustain life savings services while reinforcing resilience. The planned activities will leverage and consolidate the existing gains made by CDHI under previous NHF funding in addressing malnutrition in the selected communities.ltbrgtIn Michika and Jere LGAs, at community and PHC level, CDHI will support and strengthen outpatient therapeutic programmes (OTPs) for children 6-59 months with uncomplicated SAM, and integrate management of moderate acute malnutrition (MAM) through the Tom Brown model, and link services with micronutrient supplementation, routine immunization, and curative care for common childhood illnesses (malaria, pneumonia, diarrhea) through PHC GOPD services. In remote and hard to reach locations, outreach and or mobile services will be provided for nutrition and health interventions.ltbrgtAdditionally, PLWs who suffer acute malnutrition will benefit from supplementary nutrition assistance using Tom Browns. Community based promotion of maternal, infant, and young child nutrition - MIYCN will be integrated into the nutrition service package both at community and facility level, to ensure that prevention services are integral component of service delivery. CDHI will utilize context specific socio-behavioral change (SBCC) intervention approaches to integrate and promote hygiene, key positive household practices and gender transformation and inclusion in the communities. Consumption of locally available nutrition dense food will be promoted through cooking demonstrations during peer mother support group activities.ltbrgtEarly identification of malnutrition will be strengthened through active case finding and referrals. Care-givers and members of the communities will have their capacity strengthened on family MUAC to ensure community accountability in monitoring of nutrition status of children. CDHI will facilitate strengthening the capacity of community structures including health workers, community volunteers, and lead mothers to ensure strong linkages between both the preventive and the treatment services. Children identified with complicated SAM will be supported with transportation services to ensure timely referral to SC quick and appropriate care.ltbrgtSystem strengthening is a central focus. Local health workers will be trained and mentored in clinical protocols, supply chain management, and data reporting systems (DHIS2, LMIS), ensuring accountability and sustainability. CDHI will collaborate with State Ministries of Health, PHC Boards, and Nutrition Sector partners to strengthen coordination and progressively build government ownership while maintaining continuity of quality care. Disability inclusion and localization will be mainstreamed, ensuring meaningful participation of people with disabilities and community representatives.ltbrgtThrough this dual focus on service delivery and system strengthening, the project will sustain essential care during the lean season, protect vulnerable children and women amid funding shortfalls, and reinforce the resilience of local health systems to manage nutrition and health emergencies into the futureltbrgtlt/pgt
